newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka discussing lease of Trincomalee oil tanks.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka discussing lease of Trincomalee oil tanks.

text.p: Sri Lankan state oil firm Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Wednesday it was negotiating with a foreign company over the lease of seven to 10 small oil tanks in the northeastern town of Trincomalee.
CPC Chairman Anil Obeyesekere declined to identify the foreign company but said most details of the contract had been agreed.
The contract would be used as the basis of similar contracts for the lease of some 90 other oil tanks in Trincomalee in future, he said.

"The government is trying to finalise the lease of seven to 10 tanks to a foreign company," Obeyesekere said in an interview. "There was a Cabinet appointed tender board who went into the offer and accepted the terms and conditions and they are being now finalised."
CPC has been trying to lease 99 tanks, which each have a capacity of around 1,000 tonnes, for several years.
But the ethnic war between the Sri Lankan government and Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels, now in its 15th year, have hampered efforts to attract buyers for the tanks.
Trincomalee lies 250 km (156 miles) northeast of the capital Colombo in an area where the guerrillas have been active.
The LTTE demands a separate homeland for the minority Tamil population in the Indian Ocean island's north and east.
